architect.title: A full website audit in one click.
architect.text: A free browser extension. Open any public page, press audit, and get one weighted score across eight categories, with every failing check explained.

overview.title: Overall score
overview.text: Every audit ends in one score out of 100, with the issues that matter most listed first. Pick a category to see what it checks.
overview.alt: ARG Architect overall score and priority issues for arg.software
overview.caption: Overview

notTested.label: Not tested
notTested.text: The extension never sends attack payloads, so server-side attack classes are out of reach by design.

features.title: Security
features.text: Shows how well the page protects its visitors from the attacks a browser can actually observe: injected scripts, clickjacking, downgraded connections and leaked data. It checks the security headers the server sends, how cookies and tokens are handled, and whether API calls or client libraries expose known weaknesses. Findings are grouped by the attack each defence is meant to stop, so you can see what is unprotected and why it matters.
features.alt: ARG Architect Security report for arg.software
features.caption: Security

features.title: Performance
features.text: Shows how fast the page feels to a real visitor, from the first byte the server returns to the moment the page is usable. It measures server response, page readiness and the Core Web Vitals, taking the median of several controlled reloads in a dedicated window so one slow run does not skew the result. It also points to what is holding the page back, such as render-blocking scripts, blocking stylesheets, redirect hops and missing caching.
features.alt: ARG Architect Performance report for arg.software
features.caption: Performance

features.title: Architecture
features.text: Shows what the page depends on to work and how those pieces are connected, as far as a browser can see. It maps the third-party services, API origins and redirect chains behind the page and flags where they add risk or weight to the critical path. The technology stack is reported as a neutral profile for context and is never scored.
features.alt: ARG Architect Architecture report for arg.software
features.caption: Architecture

features.title: Efficiency
features.text: Shows how much of the page's network work is wasted. It counts the requests the page makes, finds the ones that are repeated, and estimates the bandwidth and time those duplicates cost. It also reports which HTTP versions are in use, since older ones make every request more expensive.
features.alt: ARG Architect Efficiency report for arg.software
features.caption: Efficiency

features.title: Payload
features.text: Shows what the page actually downloads during the audit and where the weight sits. Transfer size is broken down by type, covering JavaScript, images, fonts, CSS and API responses, so the heaviest part is obvious. It also checks whether assets are compressed and whether images are sized and encoded sensibly for how they are displayed.
features.alt: ARG Architect Payload report for arg.software
features.caption: Payload

features.title: Accessibility
features.text: Shows whether the page's structure lets a screen reader make sense of it and move around it. It checks the building blocks assistive technology relies on: alt text, form labels, accessible names, headings, landmarks, document language and iframe titles. It is a structural audit and does not replace keyboard, contrast or assistive-technology testing.
features.alt: ARG Architect Accessibility report for arg.software
features.caption: Accessibility

features.title: AI Readiness
features.text: Shows whether AI systems can find, read and cite the page. It checks if AI crawlers are allowed in, whether the site publishes instructions and discovery files for agents such as llms.txt, and whether the content is structured clearly enough to be extracted and quoted accurately. The aim is to see how the page is likely to be represented when someone asks an assistant about it.
features.alt: ARG Architect AI Readiness report for arg.software
features.caption: AI readiness

features.title: DOM
features.text: Shows how heavy the rendered page is for the browser to build and keep responsive. It measures the number and depth of DOM nodes, the count of external scripts, and the use of inline styles and inline event handlers. Size and depth are judged against the main-thread blocking actually measured, so a large page is only flagged when it costs responsiveness.
features.alt: ARG Architect DOM report for arg.software
features.caption: DOM

checks.title: What you can do with it

items.title: Findings you can act on
items.text: Every failing check explains the problem, names exactly what fails (the header, the file, the element, the library and its advisories), and recommends a fix. Copy any finding as a ticket draft for your issue tracker.

items.title: Export the report
items.text: Download any audit report as PDF, Markdown, or JSON, ready to attach to a ticket, share with your team, or feed into your own tooling.

items.title: Compare runs, track progress
items.text: Saved reports are grouped by day. Compare any two runs side by side, every score, check and measurement, and export the comparison too.

items.title: Audit one tab or queue ten URLs
items.text: Audits run in their own window, so your browsing is never touched, and you get a notification when the queue finishes. Cookie banners are answered with reject or essential-only, never accept.

items.label: No tracking
items.text: No account, no analytics, no tracking.

items.label: Runs locally
items.text: The language model and the vulnerability database ship inside the extension.

items.label: Only when asked
items.text: Nothing runs on the pages you browse normally; the page collectors run only on the site being audited, only during the audit.

items.label: Off by default
items.text: Optional lookups that send a hostname to a DNS service (CDN detection, AI discovery) are off by default.

review.title: Architecture review. One week on the part of your system that matters most.
review.text: €3,500 buys one week of a senior engineer, not a review of the whole application. On the architecture call we agree a scope that fits in that week, usually one slice of the product such as checkout or onboarding, and write it down before you pay. If the slice you have in mind is too big for a week, we say so and either narrow it or quote more weeks.

lists.title: What we look at, inside the agreed scope
items: System design: how the parts fit together and where the boundaries are
Code quality: structure, tests and maintainability
Scalability: where it breaks under load or data growth
Integrations: the internal and third-party APIs it depends on, and how tied you are to them
Infrastructure and operations: how it is deployed, monitored and recovered
Security: auth, tenant boundaries and data writes

lists.title: What you get
items: A written report you can forward
A map of what was reviewed: stack, data flows and integrations
A 90-day plan: do now, do later, ignore
A list of what was left out of scope, so nothing is assumed reviewed
A 60-minute readout with the engineer who wrote it
Edge findings from ARG Architect, included

review.notIncluded: anything outside the agreed scope, a pentest, a full-platform certification, an AI-citation study, a ticket-level rewrite plan.
